title: Tool-invoke micro-storyboard and compact card set for ephemeral auth flows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, mobile-first set of onboarding assets that demonstrate: (1) ephemeral credential exchange for tool-calling (short-lived keys / tokenless handoff), (2) streaming request lifecycle with progressive UI states, and (3) graceful fallback when a tool invocation fails or is rate-limited. The deliverable is a micro-storyboard (6 panels) plus a 4-card component set that can be dropped into docs, the Console onboarding modal, and SDK quickstarts. Focus constraints: keep the visual language minimal to match our docs style, ensure assets render clearly at 320px width, create Lottie-ready micro-animations for the streaming 'live' state, and provide both light + dark variants. Avoid full-page walkthroughs; aim for snippet-sized, composable visuals that can be combined with short copy. Include copy suggestions and developer-focused microcopy explaining error modes and recovery suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Six-panel micro-storyboard exported as PNGs (1x, 2x) and vector SVGs for docs use
Four compact card variants (default, streaming-live, success, fallback) with light/dark color tokens provided
Lottie JSON for the streaming-live state and a 300ms intro micro-animation for token exchange
Responsive checks: static assets legible at 320px width and desktop at 1280px
Design handoff includes copy snippets for doc headings, alt text, and suggested accessibility labels
Engineering signoff from SDK owner confirming assets map cleanly into existing doc components
attachments: Example embed mock: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/412 (WIP embed preview)

decisions: Use ephemeral-token visual metaphor (soft token chip that dissolves into request stream) rather than key icon to avoid implying long-term credentials
Provide both 'tokenless handshake' and 'ephemeral link' variants so doc writers can choose per-product messaging
Keep all micro-animations under 350KB when exported as Lottie to avoid adding bandwidth to docs pages
